state_a.description: Roundtable has enrolled Mac/Windows nodes and room seats, but no invite capability or provider-neutral join; web asks for session catalogs the hub never returns, node never publishes catalogs, Claude join is refused, Codex starts a separate app-server, and Windows currently reports WSS 521 plus Codex initialization timeout.

evidence.check: session.join and session.leave return explicit out-of-band enrollment error.
User-supplied Windows runtime report records WSS 521 and Codex initialization timeout; live capture is first selected-route step.

state_b.description: From any active room, Adrian copies one short-lived single-use invite URL, pastes it into the current Codex, Claude, or future-engine chat on an enrolled Mac/Windows node, and that exact chat joins the room without browser/admin/node secrets or a replacement agent session.

proof.expected: Exit 0 and PASS for Mac Codex current task, Windows Codex current task, Mac Claude current session, invite expiry, single use, revocation, replay refusal, no secret leakage, and no replacement child session.

authority.rule: Build universal invite/join design requested in current user message; Cloudflare 30-day correction is separate and already applied.

safety.rule: Invite is high-entropy, hashed at rest, short-lived, single-use, room-scoped, revocable, rate-limited, and redeemed only through an authenticated enrolled node; URL contains no admin, node, provider, or browser credential.

scope.rule: IN invite issue/copy/revoke, node redemption, exact current-session binding, Codex/Claude adapters, future-provider interface, Mac/Windows transport restoration, tests, deployment; OUT multi-tenant accounts, public signup, billing, session catalog as join mechanism, unrelated Roundtable defects.

quality.rule: Real pasted-link acceptance must join exact current Codex/Claude sessions on Mac/Windows, survive reconnect, refuse replay/expiry/revocation, preserve room least privilege, and prove no replacement session.

cost.rule: Reuse current hub, SQLite, node, IPC, MCP, provider adapters, and PWA with zero paid calls, new hosted services, or dependencies.

steps.operation: Restore Mac and Windows node-to-hub WSS plus installed Codex app-server initialization, then prove exact current-session identity capture for Codex and Claude without spawning a replacement session.
steps.b_state_delta: Both enrolled nodes are live and each provider has a proven exact-current-session binding contract.

steps.operation: Add invite persistence and authenticated browser issue, inspect, revoke, and consume APIs using hashed high-entropy room-scoped single-use tokens with expiry and rate limits.
steps.b_state_delta: Hub can safely issue and lifecycle-manage one room invite capability without exposing operator credentials.

steps.operation: Add node-authenticated invite redemption frames and IPC requests that atomically consume a capability and create or recover one idempotent room seat bound to the calling session.
steps.b_state_delta: An enrolled node can redeem one invite into exactly one least-privilege seat for the proven calling-session identity.

steps.operation: Build one local roundtable_join_url MCP channel with provider binders that resume the exact Codex thread, bind the exact Claude channel connection, and expose a stable adapter interface for future engines.
steps.b_state_delta: Pasting an invite into a supported current chat invokes one provider-neutral join tool and binds that exact chat to its seat.

steps.operation: Replace the dead Attach session control with an accessible Invite agent control that creates, copies, displays expiry, and revokes a room invite without exposing its token after creation.
steps.b_state_delta: Every active room has a visible Google-Meet-style invite action with secure lifecycle controls.

steps.operation: Run deterministic contract, security, reconnect, and real cross-platform pasted-link tests for Mac Codex, Windows Codex, and Claude current sessions.
steps.b_state_delta: Local and real-device evidence proves exact-session joins plus expiry, revocation, replay refusal, reconnect, and secret boundaries.

steps.operation: Deploy the verified hub, PWA, and Mac/Windows node integrations, then run production pasted-link acceptance and rollback checks.
steps.b_state_delta: Production Roundtable reaches State B with sealed live acceptance evidence and a tested rollback.

candidates.dominance_reason: Minimum expected time to verified B while keeping one capability contract, one node redemption boundary, and thin provider binders.

steps.operation: Restore cross-platform transports and prove provider session identifiers.
Add shared invite persistence and browser issue UI.
Build separate Codex and Claude redemption endpoints, local clients, and credential flows.
Add provider-specific browser instructions and controls.
steps.b_state_delta: Users can choose one provider path.

steps.operation: Test both provider-specific paths and their separate failure surfaces.
Deploy and verify both provider paths.
steps.b_state_delta: Production supports two duplicated join mechanisms.

candidates.dominance_reason: Duplicated redemption and credential surfaces increase expected rework and make future engines another full implementation.

steps.operation: Publish session catalogs and populate the browser Attach session list.
steps.b_state_delta: Browser can list provider sessions known to a node.

steps.operation: Create seats from browser-selected catalog rows.
steps.b_state_delta: Browser can attach a catalog row to a room seat.

candidates.dominance_reason: Fails target constraint: it provides browser selection, not a pasted invite that binds the exact current chat.

parallel_lanes.reason: Runtime/session proof and hub invite persistence touch independent initial surfaces.
Local provider connector and browser invite UI depend on separate completed contracts and can proceed independently.

bottleneck.resource: Real Mac and Windows provider-session identity plus transport evidence

deleted_work.reason: Catalog listing cannot bind the exact chat where invite URL was pasted.
Manual provisioning recreates current defect and fails Google-Meet-style flow.

deleted_work.item: Provider or node secrets inside invite URL
deleted_work.reason: Violates least privilege and turns copied link into a durable machine credential.

deferred_work.item: Additional engine binders beyond Codex and Claude
deferred_work.until: Stable adapter contract passes current-session acceptance for both existing providers.
Invite flow reaches production State B and a separate user need justifies catalog UI.

tether.reason: Cross-platform auth, persistence, IPC, public contract, provider adapters, and production signoff.
